title: Publish the root launcher's final X straight to latest after qualifying X-rc.N (Article 3.5, ODOC-302)
description: HELD: do not implement until the constitution Article 3.5 amendment that opum-doc is drafting is approved by the operator, first-party (Article 2.3). The ODOC id is to follow from opum-agent. Dispatched by opum-agent under OPAG-474 (opum-ai/opum-agent#1185). Operator ruling, as read from OPAG-474, from orchestrator session b8ab1ed4 at 18:45:19Z: amend Article 3.5 for the ROOT LAUNCHER only. @opum-ai/quest stages as X-rc.N under release-candidate and is qualified by opum-cli-e2e, then the final X is published straight to latest. The six platform packages stage and promote by dist-tag exactly as today. The qualified and shipped launchers must differ only by the version string, checked mechanically in CI. Motive: the npm packument readme is 0 bytes because a dist-tag move never re-derives it; only a publish onto latest does. lore-cli carries the same change, so the two flows stay paired.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The release flow stages @opum-ai/quest as X-rc.N under release-candidate for opum-cli-e2e qualification, then publishes X straight to latest, while the platform packages keep the stage-and-promote-by-dist-tag path
CI mechanically refuses unless substituting X-rc.N with X throughout the qualified rc launcher reproduces the shipped X launcher byte for byte (ODOC-302, constitution Article 3.5 at opum-doc f322cff)
After the next pair release, npm view @opum-ai/quest readme is non-empty
The flow matches lore-cli LCLI-621, confirmed with lore-cli

plan: 1. Agree the cross-repo contract with lore-cli (LCLI-621) and opum-cli-e2e, which owns both receipt schemas, before changing a reader: rc numbering, the bundle's tarball set, the pass-1 and pair receipt shapes, and what the substitution check compares

2. build-candidate-bundle: pack the launcher twice, as X-rc.N (optionalDependencies pinned to platforms at exactly X) and as X; run the substitution check in the bundle build and fail it on any non-version difference, with version-only and non-version mutants proven
3. publish-release.mjs and release.yml: stage the six platforms at X and the launcher at X-rc.N under release-candidate; keep the tag assertion (qcli385) exact
4. Readers: e2e-receipt (pass 1) and pair-receipt (pass 2) take the agreed shape; the rc launcher's integrity is checked against what npm serves

5. promote-release.mjs: platforms by dist-tag as today, then publish the bundle's X launcher with --tag latest after re-running the substitution check against the rc npm serves; rollback restores the launcher's latest by dist-tag; qcli385 admits exactly this one latest publish
6. Runbook, CHANGELOG, tests, a reviewer pass; confirm the flow matches LCLI-621 with lore-cli (AC4)

ODOC-302 has landed: opum-ai/opum-doc#500 merged 2026-09-27T19:57:51Z (merged from the operator's account; the PR carries no review record), opum-doc origin/dev f322cff; origin/main was 307c5f68 when read. Ratified text read BY REF at f322cff, docs/reference/opum-project-constitution.md (git blob 1bcff610), Article 3 clause 5. The six platform packages stage under release-candidate and reach latest by dist-tag move after qualification, quest first. The root launcher @opum-ai/quest stages as prerelease X-rc.N under release-candidate, is qualified by opum-cli-e2e, and reaches latest by a FRESH PUBLISH of X, never a dist-tag move. The qualified X-rc.N and the published X must be identical once X-rc.N is substituted for X throughout, checked mechanically in CI; the version string is the only permitted difference. A failure rolls back dist-tags, the launcher's latest included; nothing is unpublished; retry at the same version. Quest's README states no version (by design), so its substitution concerns package.json alone.

Contract agreed with lore-cli 2026-09-27 (their P1-P6 matched my proposal, which crossed with theirs). Adopted their P5 order: (a) pair receipt verifies; (b) the registry-served rc launcher, integrity-matched to the receipt, is checked against the bundle X launcher (unpacked trees, same file set, each file byte for byte after X-rc.N -> X; I also compare modes, which lore may match); (c) platforms move latest by dist-tag; (d) publish launcher X with --tag latest, quest before lore. package.json on dev and main stays at X (parity unchanged); X-rc.N exists only in the staged launcher. Quest takes the X launcher from the same quest-candidate-bundle artifact (the --qualification-run) that staging uses. P6, the receipt shape, waits on opum-cli-e2e.

Progress 2026-09-27, branch feat/QCLI-399-launcher-publish-to-latest (pushed, no PR). P4 done: scripts/qualification/launcher-equivalence.mjs compares unpacked trees entry by entry (entry set, modes, bytes after X-rc.N -> X) and asserts each package.json declares its role's version. build-candidate-bundle.mjs packs the launcher twice: tarballs/ holds the seven to stage (launcher X-rc.N plus six platforms @X), final/ holds launcher X with its own sha256.txt. The build refuses unless the two are equivalent; package-metadata.json gains a launcher block. The rc number is the registry's next free X-rc.N, overridable with --launcher-rc; an unreadable registry refuses on a release ref. Tests: qcli399 (11) plus the updated candidate-bundle tests. Mutation checks: removing the mode, entry-set or declared-version clause each fails only its own test. bun run check exit 0 (808 pass). NOT LANDABLE ALONE: publish-release.mjs, release.yml, the pass-1 gate (e2e-receipt.mjs expectedTarballNames) and the pair gate still name the launcher at X. Renaming the staged archive changes opum-cli-e2e's receipt contract, so the staging and reader half waits on their ruling, and everything lands in one PR.

opum-cli-e2e RULED 2026-09-27 (TASK-126): opum-ai/opum-cli-e2e#309 merged to their dev 20:11:22Z from head b6fd3790. Read by ref at b6fd3790, receipts/README.md (git blob 241ac885), sections "Root launcher rc-staging" and "What a reader must do". It accepts the contract, with these points binding on this side:
(1) PASS-1 per-product receipt: the tarballs entry for the launcher is keyed by its real staged filename opum-ai-quest-X-rc.N.tgz, with its real sha256. launcherVersion is REQUIRED, matching ^X-rc\.[1-9][0-9]*$ with X from the receipt's own version. New launcherSubstitution = {verdict MATCH|MISMATCH, finalTarball {filename, sha256}, method, mismatches}. It is opum-cli-e2e's OWN re-derived diff of the bundle's rc and final launchers, not a copy of our build's verdict. Reader TODO in e2e-receipt.mjs: expectedTarballNames uses the rc name; require launcherVersion; require launcherSubstitution.verdict === "MATCH" and finalTarball.sha256 equal to the bundle's final/ digest, re-derived from the bytes.
(2) PAIR receipt reader steps 5-7, on top of steps 1-4, which cover the six platforms: step 5 validates launcherVersion and checks the launcher entry's distIntegrity via npm view @opum-ai/quest@<launcherVersion>. Step 6 re-runs the substitution against what the registry serves at launcherVersion RIGHT BEFORE publishing X. Our P5(b) runs it before any tag moves; to match "immediately before", run it at P5(b) AND again just before the launcher publish, which costs one registry read of an immutable rc. Step 7 verifies after the publish that latest serves X on the launcher.
(3) opum-cli-e2e ALSO verifies the published launcher against launcherSubstitution.finalTarball after promotion. That is additive; our own pre-publish integrity check stays ours.
Nothing is left blocked. Next session: build staging (publish-release.mjs and release.yml stage the rc from tarballs/), the two readers above, promote-release.mjs P5 with the step-6 re-check, and the qcli385 exception; then the runbook, the CHANGELOG, and a reviewer pass. AC4 status 2026-09-27, per lore-cli (cross-session, against quest 629416b; their LCLI-621 part A is at lore-cli branch feat/LCLI-621-launcher-rc-final-publish 9f8f1cef, draft opum-ai/lore-cli#337). PART A MATCHES. The bundle matches in shape (lore keeps its eight tarballs flat in one artifact). Equivalence matches, modes included. Staging matches. The finalTarball.filename basename matches. One operator-experience difference, not a contract one: lore takes N from a workflow_dispatch launcher_rc input (default 1) and refuses to restage over a differing X-rc.N; quest auto-picks the next unused N. Both keep the never-reuse-N invariant. Lore has two extra equivalence clauses. Paths are compared WITHOUT substitution, which quest already does (compareTrees keys are unsubstituted). The rc must pin every platform at exactly X: quest ADOPTED this after 629416b, in launcher-equivalence.mjs with a test. PART B IS PENDING ON LORE: its promote step is not built, and that session was being recycled. Lore will adopt quest clause 4 as its spec. LORE PART B SPEC, as implemented in quest promote-release.mjs: (a) --qualification-run <id> is required; download the same bundle and gate it on the pass-1 receipt against the v<X> tag peeled commit; (b) the pair receipt, with launcherVersion equal to the bundle rc and the launcher entry keyed and read at launcherVersion; (c) dist-tags: release-candidate is X on the platforms and X-rc.N on the launcher; (d) step 6: npm pack <launcher>@X-rc.N from the registry is sha256-equal to the bundle rc, and final X equals it after substitution; (e) record the prior latest of all seven; (f) move the platforms latest by dist-tag; (g) step 6 again; (h) npm publish final/<X>.tgz --access public --tag latest, or, if X is already on npm with integrity equal to final/, a dist-tag move instead; (i) step 7: latest reads X on all seven, and npm X integrity equals final/; (j) any failure rolls back every latest this run moved, the launcher included, by dist-tag; never unpublish. The release-candidate tag test admits exactly one exception, the X launcher publish in the promote script. AC4 cannot be ticked until lore part B lands and matches.
